meaning_of_acceptance: An AI-assisted mathematical acceptance assessment of the exact bound artifacts, supported by the written proof and local checks; no external human or formal certification.
accepted_claims: For k algebraically closed of characteristic 3 and G=SL2(k), Sym^2(Sym^2 E) is the indecomposable tilting module T(4).
With t(lambda)=ch T((p-1)rho+lambda)/ch St, t(2)=z^2+z^-2 is not the character of any finite-dimensional rational G-module.
The quotient is a torus character and a virtual G-character; these and geometric interpretations are not excluded.
The cited Achar–Sobaje geometric result has been matched at statement/setup level under its stated good-characteristic and categorical hypotheses.
excluded_claims: No novelty or first-counterexample priority claim.
No independent audit of the full 56-page geometric proof or all its prerequisites.
No all-characteristic closure, bad-prime extension, or claim that all bad-prime cases are solved, false or open.
No external human review, peer-review acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification is claimed.
imported_dependencies: Standard uniqueness of the indecomposable tilting module with prescribed highest weight.
Induced/Weyl convention: nabla(n)=Sym^n E and Delta(n)=nabla(n)^* for SL2, with Sym the symmetric-power quotient.

Elementary algebraic-group background: exact diagonal-torus weight decomposition, root-subgroup generation of SL2, differentiation of rational actions, and polynomial coefficient recovery over an infinite field.
dependency_scope: The main indecomposability proof is elementary and does not require direct-summand closure for tilting modules. It does not use Smith–Treumann localization, geometric Satake, or a general tilting-character formula.
proof_mathematical_text: The public EXPLICIT_PROOF.md is byte-identical to the accepted upstream exposition. Public audit edits only change the title, AI-assistance disclosure, implementation-path reference and preparation/source-exclusion wording.
